title: Gas prices this week and what I am doing about my commute
dek: The national average for gas is around $4.42 and oil prices jumped on Monday, so the morning drive is costing more.
body: If you are filling up on the way to work this morning, you have probably noticed the number on the pump. The national average for a gallon of regular was about $4.42 at the end of last week, down only a little from the week before.

Then on Monday, oil prices jumped more than four percent as tensions overseas rose. Nobody can say exactly what that will mean at the pump, but it is a reminder that gas is one of those costs that can change quickly and hit a household budget hard.

I cannot control any of that. What I can control are a few small habits. I combine errands into one trip. I check a gas price app before filling up instead of stopping at the first station. I try to drive a little more gently on the freeway, which helps my mileage and my mood.
None of these will change the world, but together they can save a few dollars every week, and a few dollars matter right now.
Before you fill up next, check prices at two or three nearby stations. The difference is often bigger than you would expect.
